title: Customer buys from a local shop and receives it (wallet)
journey:
1. Customer signs in and sets a delivery location
2. Searches a product, opens Compare prices, picks the lowest-price delivering shop
3. Adds to cart, chooses address and delivery window, pays from wallet
4. Shop accepts, picks, packs, marks READY
5. Rider is offered automatically, accepts, enters the pickup code, starts delivery
6. Rider arrives, enters the customer's OTP - DELIVERED
7. Customer rates shop and rider
8. Admin opens the money trace: snapshot, commission, rider earning
expected: Order moves through every state with notifications at each step; wallet debited once; stock reduced; one finance snapshot; rider earning recorded; ratings saved.

title: Multi-shop cart
journey:
1. Add items from two delivering shops
2. Pay from wallet
3. Each shop fulfils independently; one is delivered, the other is rejected by the shop
expected: Two independent orders and debits; the rejected one is fully refunded with stock restored; the other completes.

title: Item unavailable - substitution
journey:
1. Place a 3-line order
2. Shop accepts, proposes a cheaper substitute for line 1 and removes line 2
3. Customer approves the substitute
4. Shop marks READY; delivery completes
expected: Difference and removed line refunded immediately; READY blocked until the customer decides; final snapshot uses the reduced goods value.

title: Shop rejects the order
journey:
1. Customer orders
2. Shop rejects with a reason
expected: Full refund, stock restored, customer notified with the reason, order never reaches a settlement.

title: No rider available
journey:
1. All riders offline; shop marks READY
2. Watch attempts until the search stops
3. A rider comes online; shop presses 'Try finding a rider again'
4. Delivery completes
expected: Bounded search with one notification at start and one at stop; restart offers the rider; order completes.

title: Rider declines / offer lapses
journey:
1. Two riders online
2. Rider 1 declines (or lets 2 minutes pass)
3. Rider 2 accepts and delivers
expected: Rider 1 is never re-offered; only one active assignment at any time.

title: Customer unavailable - failed delivery and return to shop
journey:
1. Rider picks up and starts delivery
2. Rider reports customer not reachable
3. Shop marks RETURNED
expected: Order FAILED then cancelled and refunded per policy; rider paid per the failed-delivery rule; stock restored.

title: Society authorised delivery
journey:
1. Society registered and verified; admin lists a rider and turns on exclusive riders and security notices
2. Resident joins, links an address, places an order
3. Shop marks READY
4. Only the listed rider is offered; accepts
5. Security staff notified; rider sees gate notes; delivers with OTP
expected: Dispatch honours the list; dashboard shows the delivery without PII.

title: Daily milk subscription
journey:
1. Top up the wallet
2. Subscribe to 2 L/day of milk
3. Daily-orders cron runs for the start date, then again
4. Change tomorrow to 3 L; skip the day after; pause the following two days
5. Run the cron for each date
6. Let the wallet run short one day, then top up and retry
expected: Rs 140 then Rs 210 charged once each; no order on skipped/paused days; the failed day is recovered by retry with a single debit.

title: Return and refund with rider pickup
journey:
1. Customer requests a return on a delivered order with a photo
2. Shop approves
3. Rider accepts the pickup, enters the handover code
4. Shop receives, inspects and accepts a partial amount
5. Refund completes
expected: Each status visible to the customer; wallet credited once; shop share adjusted in the next settlement; rider paid the pickup fee.

title: Cancellation at every stage (D10)
journey:
1. Place 7 orders and bring them to CONFIRMED, ACCEPTED, PREPARING, READY, ASSIGNED, PICKED_UP, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY
2. Customer tries to cancel each
3. Shop cancels the ones the customer could not
expected: Customer: allowed at CONFIRMED (full refund), blocked at four middle states, goods-only after pickup. Shop: full refund always.

title: Shop onboarding to first sale
journey:
1. New user registers a shop with identifiers and categories
2. Submits GST and PAN; operator verifies
3. Operator records the registration fee payment and approves as KESARI
4. Owner sets radius, hours, minimum order; adds products with prices and stock; uploads photos
5. A customer in range finds the shop and orders
expected: Shop goes from pending to live; appears only inside its zone; first order completes.

title: Duplicate shop registration
journey:
1. Submit a registration
2. Submit the same shop again from the same and from another account
3. Operator rejects the first
4. Owner corrects and resubmits
expected: Duplicates blocked with masked messages; resubmission updates the same record.

title: Weekly settlement and payout
journey:
1. Set commission rates
2. Complete several orders incl. one refund and one COD
3. Prepare last week's settlements and rider payouts
4. Admin approves and marks paid with references
5. Run reconciliation
expected: Batches total correctly (gross - commission - refunds +/- adjustments - COD cash held); shop and rider see their own statements; reconciliation is clean.

title: Cash on delivery
journey:
1. Shop opts in
2. Customer places a COD order under Rs 2,000
3. Rider delivers with OTP and confirms cash
4. Admin records the cash deposit
5. Weekly payout nets any cash still held
expected: Order paid on delivery; cash tracked against the rider until deposited.

title: Shop suspension with open orders
journey:
1. Shop has orders at CONFIRMED, PREPARING and OUT_FOR_DELIVERY
2. Admin previews and confirms suspension
3. Admin decides the held order
4. Admin reinstates the shop
expected: Policy applied per status; owner informed; customers cannot order meanwhile; reinstatement restores service.

title: Marketing campaign with consent
journey:
1. Two customers order from the shop; one grants marketing consent
2. Shop builds a segment and a campaign, submits it
3. Operator approves; shop sends
4. Consenting customer opens it and orders
5. Customer withdraws consent; shop sends another campaign
expected: Only the consenting customer is messaged; conversion tracked; nothing after withdrawal.

title: Risk flag to suspension
journey:
1. Create a risk condition (e.g. repeated wrong delivery codes)
2. Run the rules
3. Operator reviews and suspends from the flag
4. Admin reinstates
expected: One flag raised; suspension applied with notice; flag closed with the reason.

title: New customer: mobile sign-up to first order
journey:
1. Sign up with an unused mobile + email
2. Complete details and geo-tagged address
3. Top up the wallet
4. Place and receive an order
expected: Account, wallet and address created; order completes without extra prompts.

title: Multi-role user
journey:
1. A shop owner applies as a rider and is approved
2. Switches role and delivers an order for another shop
3. Switches back and fulfils an order in the own shop
4. Places a personal order as a customer
expected: Each role works in turn; data stays separated by role.

title: Order from a closed shop
journey:
1. Shop is closed
2. Customer confirms the closed-shop prompt and pays
3. Shop opens
expected: Both parties alerted immediately and once more at opening; order then proceeds normally.

title: Price governance
journey:
1. Admin sets an MRP
2. Owner tries to price above it by form and Excel
3. Operator proposes a price change; owner approves
4. Customer sees the new price and discount
5. Owner changes the MRP of one product for the own shop (NEW-010)
6. Customer compares the product across two shops
expected: MRP guard holds on every path; approval flow gates the operator's change. The owner's MRP change shows for that shop only; the other shop and the master keep theirs.

title: New shop stocks up by category and makes its first sales
journey:
1. Shop C (approved, no products) adds a product category
2. Owner opens the inventory: every product of the category is there at stock 100
3. Owner opens the 'needs price' list and sets prices for products that had none, including one loose product
4. Owner corrects two stock figures to the real count
5. Customer finds the shop, buys one packaged product and 500 g of the loose product
6. Shop accepts, picks, packs; rider delivers
7. Owner checks inventory, movements and the sales figure
expected: All products added once at 100; unpriced ones not buyable until priced; the order is charged at the shop prices; stock falls by exactly what was sold; movements and revenue match the order.

title: Loose goods: from no price to a sale
journey:
1. Operator creates a loose product in the master
2. Shops A and B add it; both see an empty price
3. Customer sees both as price not set and cannot add either
4. Shop B sets Rs 60 per kg; Shop A leaves it empty
5. Customer compares, buys 750 g from Shop B
6. Shop B clears the price again
expected: No Rs 0 is ever shown or charged. Only the priced shop is buyable. The order is Rs 45 exactly. After the price is cleared the product is no longer buyable.

title: Shop-specific MRP
journey:
1. Shops A and B sell the same packaged product, master MRP Rs 50
2. Owner A changes the MRP to Rs 55 and the price to Rs 52
3. Customer compares both shops
4. Admin changes the master MRP to Rs 60
5. Customer buys from each shop
6. Owner A tries to change the MRP of Shop B through the API
expected: Shop A shows MRP 55 throughout; Shop B follows the master (50, then 60). Each order records the MRP and price of its own shop. The cross-shop change is refused.

title: Sell, purchase and inventory reconcile over a day
journey:
1. Note opening stock for three Shop A products
2. Owner records stock received for one product
3. Customers place five orders: one delivered normally, one cancelled, one with a substitution, one with a removed line, one delivered then returned
4. Owner writes off damaged stock
5. Owner records an in-shop sale
6. At the end compare inventory, movements, shop sales and the admin money trace
expected: For each product: closing stock = opening + received - sold - written off + returned to stock. Sales count delivered goods only. Wallet debits and refunds match the orders. Every stock change has a movement.

title: Log out and log off on a shared phone
journey:
1. Shop owner signs in on a phone browser, works in the shop portal, signs out
2. Back button and a saved /shop link are tried
3. A customer signs in on the same browser, shops and signs out
4. The owner signs in again
5. A session is left idle past its lifetime
expected: After each log out nothing of the previous user is visible or reachable. Each user finds the own cart and data on return. The idle session is ended and returns to the page asked for after sign-in.

title: Field validation along the first-order journey
journey:
1. New user enters an invalid then a valid mobile, email and code
2. Enters invalid then valid profile and address fields (name, recipient mobile, PIN, map pin)
3. Tops up with an invalid then a valid amount and voucher code
4. Adds an invalid then a valid quantity to the cart
5. Places the order with notes and delivery instructions
expected: Every invalid entry is stopped at its field with a clear message and typed values are kept. Nothing invalid is saved. The valid path completes with one order and one debit.

title: Order paid online, invoiced and refunded to source
journey:
1. Customer checks out and pays by UPI
2. Shop fulfils; rider delivers with a photo
3. Customer downloads the tax invoices
4. Customer returns one item; refund is approved
5. Admin runs reconciliation
6. A second customer abandons the payment page
expected: Paid order moves CAPTURED -> RECONCILED; invoices match the order; the refund goes to the source with a credit note; the abandoned payment leaves no order, no charge and no stock held.

title: Mobile sign-up by SMS and messages on every channel
journey:
1. New user signs up with a mobile and the SMS code
2. Enters a wrong code first
3. Switches on SMS, WhatsApp and push
4. Places an order through to delivery
5. Switches WhatsApp off and orders again
expected: Wrong code refused; right code signs in with the mobile verified. Each switched-on channel delivers each event once; the switched-off channel stays silent.

title: Shop onboarding with KYC documents and fee gate
journey:
1. Owner registers and uploads KYC documents, one of them invalid
2. Operations reject that document; owner re-uploads
3. Operator tries to approve before the fee is paid
4. Fee is recorded and verified; operator approves
5. Customer finds the shop
expected: Invalid document refused; state moves KYC_PENDING -> PAYMENT_PENDING -> VERIFIED -> ACTIVE; approval is blocked until the fee is verified; the shop is listed only when ACTIVE.

title: Multi-shop purchase with coupon, scheduled slot and master order
journey:
1. Customer fills a cart from two shops
2. Tries an expired coupon, then a valid one
3. Chooses a scheduled slot; a full slot is refused
4. Pays
5. One shop rejects its order
expected: One master reference with two child orders; discount applied once; slot carried on both; only the rejected part is refunded, in proportion.

title: Shop does not accept in time
journey:
1. Customer places a wallet order, an online order and a COD order with one shop
2. The shop accepts none before the timeout
expected: All three are cancelled automatically once: wallet credited, online refunded to source, COD nothing; stock restored; customer and shop notified.

title: Rider profile edit, batching and photo proof
journey:
1. Rider changes bank details with the confirmation code
2. Two nearby orders become READY and are batched to the rider
3. Rider delivers both with a photo each
4. Operations block the rider afterwards
expected: Bank change waits for verification before any payout; both orders delivered with their own codes and photos; the blocked rider gets no further offers.

title: Customer referral
journey:
1. Customer 1 shares the referral code
2. A new customer signs up with it and gets a first order delivered
3. Customer 1 then tries to refer an own second account on the same phone
expected: First referral rewards both once after delivery. The self-referral earns nothing and raises a risk flag.

title: Release check on both sites
journey:
1. The release reaches test.gokesari.com
2. The production-safe and signed-in tiers run there; defects are fixed and re-deployed
3. The release reaches gokesari.com
4. The production-safe tier runs there
5. The register is rebuilt
expected: The same suite commit has a staging run and a production run in docs/testing/qa-runs, and the register shows each case's status on both sites.

title: Signed-in test run by the Claude QA agent
journey:
1. The agent signs the staging test accounts in with the emailed codes (owner's mailbox)
2. It runs the signed-in tier on test.gokesari.com
3. It collects the results and rebuilds the register
expected: A staging run with signed-in checks that passed (so the sessions worked), collected into docs/testing/qa-runs.

title: Identity-first shop registration to first sale
journey:
1. New user opens /shop/register, verifies the GSTIN with consent
2. Confirms owner / address, pins the shop on the map, fills shop details and turnover slab
3. Reviews and pays the fee in the sandbox
4. Sees the live screen and e-mail; downloads the product template
5. Uploads 10 products (2 bad rows), fixes them
6. Customer at the PIN finds the shop, orders, shop fulfils, rider delivers
expected: Shop live immediately after payment; bad rows explained and the rest imported; only Live listings visible; the first order completes end to end.
preconditions: New test user, a staging-verifiable GSTIN, Cashfree sandbox data, a customer at the shop's PIN.

title: PAN-only pharmacy with a licence on the promise: notice, reminder, suspension
journey:
1. Register with PAN, declaration and consent; pick a pharmacy shop type
2. Read the drug-licence 90-day notice; tick the promise on the documents screen; pay; shop goes live
3. Receive the grace e-mail and a follow-up reminder
4. Let the grace end; the follow-up run suspends the shop
5. Customer opens the shop page
expected: Go-live not blocked; e-mails sent with the right dates; automatic suspension with admin notice; customers see the shop is not taking orders.
preconditions: New test user, a staging-verifiable PAN (may be Blocked by defect D2), pharmacy shop type; grace shortened with the developer. A food shop no longer fits this journey: FSSAI is must-have before paying since DF-08 (PR #467, TC-DOC-020, TC-DOC-021).

title: Delivery partner: DigiLocker KYC to first withdrawal
journey:
1. Applicant verifies PAN and Aadhaar (DigiLocker mock); admin approves
2. Rider delivers orders and earns
3. Adds a bank account; Secure ID verifies it
4. Withdraws ₹100 with the e-mailed code
5. Monthly payout runs; TDS checked against the 194C limits
expected: Aadhaar kept masked; withdrawal within limits paid by IMPS with no fee; monthly payout by NEFT; TDS only above the limits.
preconditions: Rider payout flags ON on staging; DigiLocker mock; Cashfree sandbox bank data.

title: Dealer chain earns tiered commission on a new shop
journey:
1. Prospect requests a referral code; the agent shares his dealer code
2. Shop registers with the code applied and pays the ₹4,999 slab
3. Commission records for agent, lead and main dealer; the agent's dashboard updates live
4. Payout on the 5th (“Close <Month YYYY> now”) with payee checks
expected: ₹999.80 / ₹199.96 / ₹149.97 (20 / 4 / 3 %) earned at activation; held where agreement, PAN or bank is missing; paid otherwise.
preconditions: Dealer programme and tiered commission ON on staging; agent → lead → main dealer chain.

title: Dealer network month: targets, promotion, development bonus, reports, close and reversal
features: DLR-TIER, DT-18, DT-19, DT-20, DT-21, DT-22, DT-23
journey:
1. During the month shops activate under agents and leads; dashboards and team performance update
2. Daily report next morning; weekly report on Monday
3. An agent reaches 50 shops and 3 ready agents and is promoted
4. A renewal is paid; one shop is refunded
5. Month close on the 5th: bonuses, development check, one payout per person
expected: Shares 20 / 4 / 3 %; target bonus only at 50+; development bonus only with 100+ team shops; renewal 10 / 2 / 1 %; refund reverses every level; one payout per person with gross / TDS / net.
preconditions: TIERED chain on staging with seeded month data (developer); PR #417 on staging for the 3% parts.

title: New shop fills its shelf: starter shelf, barcode, Excel update
journey:
1. Set how the shop delivers and its radius
2. Publish the starter shelf
3. Scan one known and one unknown barcode
4. Update prices and stock with the Excel file (with some bad rows)
5. Customer browses the shop
expected: Listings Live with correct prices; unknown barcode sent for approval; bad Excel rows explained; customer sees only Live listings within the radius.
preconditions: A newly live shop with one category; a phone with camera.

title: Shop day on Billing v2: POS, online orders, returns and GST
journey:
1. Shop makes POS sales, some offline
2. Online orders delivered; one partial return
3. Purchases recorded
4. Month-end: GSTR-1 / 3B prepared, 2B reconciled, Tally export
expected: Bills numbered without gaps; credit note for the return; TCS / TDS correct; GSTR-1 / 3B prepared from the books (totals match the portal's after Save); 2B reconciled; the Tally export reads back unchanged.
preconditions: billing_v2 and related flags ON for the test district (else Not Applicable).

title: Assisted registration: a dealer registers a shop and the owner pays on their phone (planned WP7)
journey:
1. Dealer chooses Register for someone and enters the owner's mobile
2. Owner gives consent by OTP or link
3. Dealer fills the wizard on the owner's draft with his code locked
4. Owner pays on their own phone by QR / UPI or the pay link
5. Shop goes live; map pin and starter shelf done with the owner
expected: Consent recorded; helper never pays; shop live after the owner's payment; dealer credited; every helper step audited.
preconditions: Assisted mode on staging (R4).

title: PAN-only owner registers on a phone in Marathi with scan and DigiLocker (planned WP8, WP10)
journey:
1. Owner switches to मरा and finds a dealer by PIN
2. Scans the PAN card; status chip shows Checking… then the result
3. Verifies identity with DigiLocker
4. Pins the shop, pays the fee, goes live
expected: Every screen in Marathi (English fallback, never blank); PAN read by scan; Aadhaar never stored; shop live after payment.
preconditions: Wave 2 / 3 on staging; DigiLocker live or mock.
origin: Planned - R4 / R5, not built yet (20-Nov-2026)

title: Abandoned registration: reminders, dealer notice, restart
journey:
1. Owner stops at the Address step
2. Reminder after 24 h and again after 72 h idle; dealer told at 72 h
3. After 7 days the draft is abandoned
4. Owner opens /shop/register again
expected: Reminders and dealer notice at the right times; restart at screen 1 after 7 days; no reminders once paid.
preconditions: A registration started with a dealer code; time shortened with the developer on staging.

title: Territory dealer: territory, fee, rating, order income and payout
journey:
1. Admin gives the dealer a territory (exclusive pincodes, yearly fee)
2. Dealer pays the fee online (sandbox) and the territory becomes Active
3. Daily rating; customers order from shops in the territory; one goods refund
4. The dealer's card shows this month's orders and income
5. Month close: TERRITORY entry, one payout on the 5th with 'Territory order income'
6. Rule switched off again
expected: Pincodes held exclusively; Active only after the webhook; share 20-25% by rating; refunds netted; one payout with the territory line; nothing else changes while the rule is off.
preconditions: Rule territoryDealer switched on for the test on staging; a TIERED test dealer; test shops in the test pincodes; sandbox payments; month close with the developer.

title: Team lead grows his team; the main dealer promotes an agent
journey:
1. Team lead adds an agent from /dealer; the main dealer is told
2. The new agent signs shops with his own code (sandbox); commission waits until his account is linked and the agreement accepted
3. An agent reaches 50 shops and 3 ready agents
4. The main dealer promotes him from /dealer
5. Month close with >= 100 shops from the new team
expected: Agent added at once under the lead; 20 / 4 / 3 % on his shops; promotion only when eligible, recruits move with him; former lead's 1% development bonus only in months with >= 100 shops.
preconditions: A TIERED chain main dealer > team lead > agent with linked accounts; promotion counts arranged with the developer on staging.

title: Book a consultant, pay at the visit, complete with the code
journey: Consultant publishes → customer finds and books (pay at visit) → consultant records payment → completes with the customer's code → customer rates
expected: Booking CONFIRMED → PAID (receipt) → COMPLETED; commission line in the next payout; rating on the profile.
preconditions: Rule consultBooking switched on (Admin → Settings).

title: Book online, cancel, refund
journey: Customer books paying online (sandbox) → cancels before the free-cancellation time
expected: Hold → CONFIRMED/PAID → CANCELLED with a full refund in progress; the time is free again.
preconditions: Rule consultBooking switched on (Admin → Settings). Sandbox gateway.

title: New shop → paid → live → welcome kit e-mail → banner downloaded again → QR opens the shop
journey:
1. A new owner registers a shop in the wizard and pays the fee (sandbox)
2. The shop goes live
3. The welcome e-mail arrives with both banners and print instructions
4. The owner downloads the banners from Seller Central → Marketing
5. The QR code on the banner opens the shop's page
expected: One welcome e-mail with the English and the local-language banner (PDFs attached); the Marketing downloads match; the QR opens <site>/shops/<slug>.
preconditions: PAYMENT_GATEWAY=SANDBOX; e-mail delivery configured.

title: Puja Samagri shop from registration to first delivered order, with the staff side, the welcome kit and the mailbox pool
features: PUJA-02, PUJA-04, PUJA-05, PUJA-08, PUJA-09, PUJA-10, PUJA-12, ADMNAV-02, WKIT-02, MAILPOOL-01
journey:
1. Admin: Categories → Shop → “Shop types with their own setup” → “Puja Samagri” → “Festivals”; creates “Diwali puja kits” (now to tomorrow, IST, home banner)
2. New user registers a shop of type “Puja Samagri & Temple Supplies” in Pune and pays the fee
3. The welcome e-mail arrives in testing@gokesari.com with the English and Marathi banners; email_mailbox_sends shows its SENT row
4. At “7. Add your products” the owner keeps Kapur, Phool & Patte and Ready Puja Kits and takes them at stock 100
5. The owner creates an own product “Pooja Chunni <run>” (confirming past close names)
6. Operator: Catalogue → Shop categories → “Puja Samagri” → “Review queue”; approves it
7. Customer opens /puja in मराठी, sees the festival banner with kits first, searches “कापूर”
8. Customer asks the price of a loose flower; owner sets ₹60 on “Price requests”
9. Customer orders a kapur pack and the flower, pays online (sandbox); shop packs; rider delivers with the OTP
10. Customer places a wallet order and cancels it before packing
expected: Shop live after payment; one welcome e-mail, sent from a pool mailbox, whose banners carry “Everything For Everyone, Everywhere” / “सर्वांसाठी सर्व काही, सर्वत्र” and “आपले दुकान आता ऑनलाइन”. The three categories listed at stock 100 (loose items waiting for a price). The own product listed at once, then in the master after approval (“Your product was approved”). Marathi search and kits-first work; the flower is sold at the confirmed ₹60; order 1 DELIVERED with the OTP and stock down; order 2 refunded in full to the wallet with its stock back. Staff reached every page without Shops-menu tiles.
preconditions: test.gokesari.com; a new test user and a staging-verifiable GSTIN; Puja Samagri type ON; the fee paid on the sandbox page; a customer at the shop's PIN with Cashfree sandbox data (UPI testsuccess@gocash) and wallet balance; admin, operator and a rider; EMAIL_POOL set and staging mail redirected to testing@gokesari.com; read-only database access.

title: Food shop signup under DF-08: FSSAI before payment, Shop Act on the promise, staff upload for a second owner
journey:
1. Owner A verifies the GSTIN, address, map pin and shop details for a Bakery and reads the FSSAI notice
2. Clicks “Create my shop and pay”: “Upload your documents” holds the payment until FSSAI is uploaded
3. Uploads the FSSAI certificate (checked with Cashfree sandbox), ticks the promise for the Shop Act and pays
4. The shop goes live; no 90-day FSSAI e-mail; on the next reminder day the reminder names only the promised Shop Act
5. Owner A uploads the Shop Act; the next run sends nothing
6. Owner B (Dairy Shop) stops at “Upload your documents” and sends the FSSAI licence to GoKesari
7. The admin uploads it on /admin/shops/<B>/documents with the on-behalf consent
8. Owner B's screen goes on; B promises the Shop Act, pays and goes live
expected: Neither food shop can pay without FSSAI (FSSAI_REQUIRED on the screen and at checkout). A goes live with FSSAI on file and the promise recorded (due + 90 days), gets no FSSAI grace e-mail, is reminded only for the Shop Act with the promise wording, and the reminders stop once it is uploaded. B is unblocked by the staff upload, recorded under the admin, and goes live on payment.
preconditions: Two new test users; staging-verifiable GSTINs and referral codes; shop types Bakery and Dairy Shop; test FSSAI certificates with the Cashfree sandbox number 10121002000677 and a future expiry; Sandbox payment (“Pay (success)” while PAYMENT_GATEWAY=SANDBOX); the staging admin; developer help to trigger the follow-up on a reminder day.

title: A doctor joins GoKesari Health: medical registration on the promise, found by group and plain words
journey:
1. The doctor registers a Consultant / Professional Firm (appointments) shop in the wizard, promises the Shop Act and pays
2. On “7. What does your shop sell?” picks Cardiologist under Health — Specialists
3. Legal documents shows “Medical registration” (Required, Upload by 20 Feb 2027); Shops missing documents lists it as due
4. The doctor uploads the registration with the council and sets up the Cardiologist booking profile
5. The operator verifies the doctor in Admin → Health → Verification
6. The admin opens Health → Specialties: Cardiologist counts the doctor and the shop
7. The customer opens Find a doctor → Specialists → “Cardiologist · Heart”, then types “heart”, and books
expected: The medical registration is asked by the Doctors rule with legalDocuments off, never blocks orders, and stops being chased once submitted. The Specialties tab counts the new doctor and shop. The customer finds the verified cardiologist through the group chip, the specialty chip and plain words; an unverified doctor never appears.
preconditions: Rules health and consultBooking ON; rule legalDocuments OFF; a new test user with a staging-verifiable GSTIN or PAN; a test medical registration certificate; the staging admin and operator; the staging customer.

title: Buy a franchise zone with pay-first KYC and earn on the first team shop
features: FRN-02, FRN-04, FRN-05, FRN-06, FRN-08, FRN-11, FRN-12, FRN-13, FRN-15
journey:
1. Guest opens /franchise/book, selects GKZ-PUN-17 “Pune – Koregaon Park–Mundhwa”, taps Continue and “Sign in to pay”
2. Signs in and lands on the priced cart (₹1,50,000 + GST ₹27,000 = ₹1,77,000); gives name, mobile and PAN, accepts the rules (2026-11-22), reserves and pays
3. /franchise/my shows “Booked · awaiting KYC” with the 30-day due date; no franchise code yet
4. Opens /dealer/apply: the zone is his working area; verifies PAN and GSTIN online, the bank with the bank, the mobile; accepts the agreement and submits
5. Admin approves the application; the franchise goes live and a GKF- code is issued
6. The owner adds an agent on /dealer; the agent registers a shop with his code at PIN 411036 (area Mundhwa), pays the ₹999 fee; admin approves
7. One-time commission: agent ₹199.80, owner ₹39.96 (case B2)
8. A customer orders ₹10,000 from the shop; it is delivered
9. The owner's live month shows rate 20.0% and ₹40 recurring; after month end the month is locked and paid on the 5th
expected: The zone is his from the payment but earns only after KYC; every amount comes from the server; B2 one-time and 20%-of-2% recurring are paid by GoKesari directly to each person; no screen shows another owner's data.
preconditions: New test user without a dealer account; owner-agreed test PAN / GSTIN; Cashfree sandbox bank-verification test data; staging payment page or Cashfree sandbox; admin account; flag dealer_programme_enabled ON; a customer at PIN 411036; nothing sold yet in GKZ-PUN-17.

title: Free dealership in a zone, then upgrade to a paid franchise; a free team keeps working in the paid zone
features: FRN-04, FRN-05, FRN-07, FRN-11, FRN-12, FRN-13
journey:
1. User selects GKZ-PUN-29 and chooses “Free dealership”; /dealer/apply?zone=GKZ-PUN-29 saves it as his working zone; he applies and is approved
2. His agent registers a shop in Sahakar Nagar (GKZ-PUN-29) and it is approved: case A2 — agent ₹199.80, dealer ₹39.96
3. On /dealer he taps “Upgrade to Paid Franchise”, books GKZ-PUN-29 with coupon QA10 (₹1,59,300) and pays; it is live at once
4. His earlier team shop attaches to the franchise (UPGRADE); a new team shop is case B2 — agent ₹199.80, owner ₹39.96
5. The other free dealer's agent registers a shop in Balaji Nagar (GKZ-PUN-29): case A2 for that team, no one-time to the owner
6. Orders are delivered from all three shops; the month is calculated and locked
expected: No shop is paid twice; shops registered before the upgrade keep their Model A plans; from going live the owner earns 20% of GoKesari's 2% on his own-team shops and on the free team's shop in his zone (he is its only owner).
preconditions: Test user without a dealer account; a second approved free dealer with an agent; coupon QA10; staging payment page or Cashfree sandbox; admin; flag dealer_programme_enabled ON.

title: Referral moves: a shop and a team member change franchise team with consent letters and a second admin
features: REFM-01, REFM-02, REFM-03, REFM-04, REFM-05, REFM-06
journey:
1. Admin A opens Admin → Dealers → Referral moves, finds SH and raises a request to move it to Y's agent with a reason
2. Admin A raises a member request moving G1 under Y's team lead
3. Admin A uploads the shop owner's, X's and Y's letters (and G1's, X's, Y's for the member)

5. Orders are delivered from SH after the move; the month is calculated
6. Read the ledger, the team periods, G1's code and the audit log

title: New Business Partner dealer: choose, pay, get approved, earn one-time and monthly, change scheme
features: DPLT-02, DPLT-03, DPLT-04, DPLT-05, DPLT-09, DPLT-12
journey:
1. New user opens /dealer/apply, saves details, compares schemes and chooses Business Partner
2. Pays ₹12,980 on the sandbox page, accepts the agreement and the scheme's terms, submits
3. Admin approves: GKD code, assignment Business Partner v1
4. A shop registers with the code, pays and is approved
5. ₹1,00,000 of orders are delivered; the month is closed
6. The dealer opens /dealer: scheme card and earnings; then moves to Free Dealership
7. Admin opens the dealer dashboard and the dealer's Scheme history
expected: Payment counted only on the sandbox confirmation; acceptance recorded with the terms' fingerprint; ₹249.75 one-time at shop approval and ₹300 monthly (15% of ₹2,000) at the month close, paid with the month's payout; the downgrade applies at once without changing earned lines; the dashboard counts the dealer under Business Partner and the ₹11,000 joining charge in platform revenue until the change.

title: Photo shopping list to delivered orders from two shops
features: SMART-01, SMART-02, SMART-03, SMART-04, SMART-05, SMART-10
journey:
1. Customer taps “Scan my shopping list” on the home page and photographs a 2-page handwritten Marathi list
2. Fixes one low-confidence product and one quantity, names the list and taps “Save & compare shop prices”
3. Sorts by Lowest total, opens “Compare item by item” and taps “Order from this shop” on the cheapest shop
4. Goes to the cart and pays
5. The shop gets the order on WhatsApp and taps Accept
6. The shop packs; the rider picks up and delivers with the customer's OTP
7. Customer taps “Order the N not-ordered items from another shop”, orders them from the second shop and pays
8. After 30 days the list photo is purged
expected: Items and quantities read correctly; the wishlist is saved with its photo; only shops within 3 km are compared with correct pack maths, totals and delivery options; the cart holds exactly the available items at the compared prices and any change is reported; each shop's order runs through payment, acceptance (WhatsApp Accept equals the app's), delivery and settlement unchanged; the not-ordered items are bought from the second shop; the photo is deleted and the wishlist stays.
preconditions: test.gokesari.com with flags smart_list_scan_enabled (and whatsapp_shop_orders_enabled for step 5) ON; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set (Blocked until the owner adds it) and the Meta WhatsApp set-up for step 5. Staging customer with a Pune location and wallet balance or Cashfree sandbox data (card 4111 1111 1111 1111, OTP 111000); two shops within 3 km that sell different items of the list; an approved online rider.

title: Shop owner's new tools: logo, product by photo, price and offer by voice — then a sale
features: CF-011, SMART-07, SMART-08, VPA-01, VPA-02, VPA-04, VPA-05, VPA-06
journey:
1. Owner opens My Shop → Open / close, hours and uploads a square shop logo
2. Inventory → Add product by photo: photographs a packed product's front, back, label and barcode and taps Read photos
3. Types or says “₹60 per litre, 50 bottles”, checks the read-back, uses the catalogue match (or adds it new) and taps Publish to my shop
4. Inventory → Change price or offer by voice: says “<product> 10 टक्के सूट रविवार पर्यंत”, checks what GoKesari understood and taps Yes, publish
5. Says “<product> price 9000 rupees”, sees the big-rise warning and taps “No, change it”
6. Customer opens the shop: sees the logo on the shop card, the new product and the offer price; orders and pays by wallet
7. Owner stops the offer in Marketing → Offers
expected: The logo shows on the shop card; the product is live in the shop (a new product waits for admin review for other shops) with the per-bottle price, stock in the stock ledger and photos through the photo pipeline; the voice offer is a normal shop offer ending Sunday 23.59 IST and the customer pays 10% less until it is stopped; the 9000 price is warned and never published; every change has its price-history or audit row and nothing changes without the owner's Yes.
preconditions: test.gokesari.com with shop_logo_upload_enabled and voice_price_assistant_enabled ON (as on 23-Nov-2026) and shop_photo_listing_enabled ON for the shop's district; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for the photo read (Blocked until set). Staging shop owner; a customer in the shop's area with wallet balance.

title: Accountant to CA: journal, bank reconciliation and a rate change through to activation
journey:
1. Accountant drafts a ₹1.00 journal (Dr 1010 QA bank / Cr 4990 QA income) and submits it to the CA
2. Accountant tries to approve it; the CA approves it in To approve
3. Accountant checks the statement file, then imports and matches it
4. Matches the ₹1.00 credit to the posted journal and excludes the ₹0.50 charge with a reason
5. Submits the statement; the CA signs it off
6. Downloads the reconciliation CSV and tries to delete the statement
7. Accountant proposes a default commission change effective now; the CA approves; the admin activates it on Admin → Approvals
8. Trial balance and Admin → Finance are checked
expected: Self-approval refused (403); the journal is POSTED by the CA; the statement BS-… is RECONCILED and final (delete → 409); the CSV downloads; the rate is ACTIVATED only after the CA and the admin and the default commission changes through the existing setter; the trial balance has debits = credits; every step is audited.
preconditions: test.gokesari.com; flag `rbac_v2_accounting` ON; gk-ops acting as Accountant, gk-oplim acting as CA; an admin (and a second admin while `rbac_v2_four_eye_admin` is ON); a CSV statement with one ₹1.00 receipt and one ₹0.50 bank charge for a fresh account name such as “QA run … ••0000”.

title: Operations task to Support to the shop owner and back: the handover closes
journey:
1. Operations Manager assigns a Follow-up task on shop A to the Operations User
2. Operations User starts it and raises a support ticket from the task
3. Support Manager assigns the ticket to the same person, who holds Support User as a grant while acting as Operations User
4. As Support User: open the shop workbench from My tickets, propose a description change and a price change, send to the owner
5. Shop owner approves all on /shop/changes
6. Operations User confirms the resolved ticket in Raised by me and marks the task Done with an outcome
7. Admin reads the ticket, approval and task histories
expected: The ticket is linked to the task; the assignment is accepted (PR #500); the ticket goes Awaiting Shop Owner → Resolved after the owner approves; the changes are live only after approval; the Operations User is told at each step; “Confirm and close” → Closed; the task is DONE; all three histories are complete and append-only.
preconditions: Flags `rbac_v2_operations`, `rbac_v2_support` and `rbac_v2_shop_change_requests` ON; gk-ops (Operations Manager + Support Manager) and gk-oplim (Operations User + Support User) put in both teams on Admin → Staff teams; shop A and its owner's account.

title: New shop (wizard, dealer link or admin on behalf) → sandbox fee → live → one personalised welcome e-mail → both QRs scan
journey:
1. Register a shop in the owner's wizard, through a dealer's fee link, and by an admin on the owner's behalf; pay each with the sandbox 'Pay (success)'
2. Each shop goes live
3. Read the testing inbox: one e-mail per shop, 'Dear <owner>, congratulations! <shop> is now live on GoKesari.com'
4. Open the EN and MR banners (HI for a shop outside Maharashtra): owner line, headline, Order online QR, Pay here (UPI) QR when the shop has a UPI ID
5. Scan both QRs with a phone
6. Admin: Resend updated banner for one shop; bulk send to all live shops
expected: One personalised e-mail per shop with both banners; the shop QR opens the shop (app when installed), the UPI QR opens a UPI app with the shop as payee and no amount; resend gives one updated-banner e-mail; bulk counts sent and skipped.
preconditions: test.gokesari.com, PAYMENT_GATEWAY=SANDBOX, mail redirected to the testing inbox, flag shop_welcome_kit_admin_send_enabled on.
